messages:
emily_cust: Hey team — enterprise customer hitting 400 from /v1/embeddings in prod. Error says 'Invalid embedding shape'. Works when they run locally. Pasting a redacted request body below and the client they use (custom JS wrapper).

ryan_support: Thanks — can you paste the exact request body (no PII) and the model name + client lib version? Also does the error come back synchronously or as a 422/400?

emily_cust: Body (redacted):
```json
{
  "model": "text-embed-2025-small",
  "input": [ [ [0.012, 0.223, 0.998, ..., 0.001] ] ]
}
```
Response: 400, body: `{\"error\": \"Invalid embedding shape: expected (1536,) or (n,1536), got (1,1,1536)\"}`

jordan_dev: That is the issue — the client is double-wrapping the vector. The API expects either a single embedding as a 1D array (i.e. `input: [0.012, ...]`) when sending one embedding OR a batch as a 2D array `input: [[...],[...]]`. Your payload is 3D: `[[[...]]]` which becomes shape (1,1,1536).

ingrid_eng: Repro'd quickly with curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-2025-small","input":[[[0.01,0.02,0.03,...]]]}'
# => 400 Invalid embedding shape: got (1,1,1536)
```
Fix: flatten one level. For single vector: `{"model":"text-embed-2025-small","input":[0.01,0.02,...]}`. For a batch of two: `{"model":"...","input":[[...],[...]]}`.

ryan_support: Common causes we see:
- The client code wraps batched payloads with an extra array for singleton handling (like `if not list_of_vectors: list_of_vectors = [list_of_vectors]`) but then later wraps again when building the request.
- Libraries that convert numpy arrays to lists incorrectly (e.g., `json.dumps(str(np_array))`) turning arrays into strings.
- Serializing `'Content-Type': 'text/plain'` by accident so server treats JSON as string and errors propagate poorly.

jordan_dev: Quick Python snippet to fix on client side:
```py
# make sure `vectors` is a list-of-floats or list-of-list-of-floats
if isinstance(vectors[0], list):
    payload_input = vectors  # already batched
else:
    payload_input = vectors  # single vector as 1D list
# ensure top-level is correct form for API
payload = {"model": model_name, "input": payload_input}
```
(If you have a single vector stored as `[0.1,0.2,...]`, do NOT wrap into `[[[...]]]`).

emily_cust: Patch applied on the customer wrapper, they removed the extra wrap and retested — now 200 OK. They also reported a latency spike when sending huge batches (256 vectors) so we left a note.

ingrid_eng: For throughput: recommend batching in the client to 32–64 vectors per request for our default GPU configs; larger batches increase tail latency and may trigger queuing/batching heuristics, which can look like amplifying latency under concurrency. Also if vectors are precomputed, sending compressed formats or using binary protocols helps but requires private deployments.

ryan_support: Follow-ups: 1) customer fixed; 2) I filed an internal ticket to improve the error message to hint at nested-array shapes (ENG-4567). 3) Added a small snippet to the JS wrapper docs about not double-wrapping and appropriate batching limits. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployed docs change to https://docs.redwood.ai/reference/embeddings (patch d2f4c9)

emily_cust: Thanks all — closing on our side. Will re-open if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
